Chapter 10: Sustaining Excellence—Embedding Principles for the Long Haul.
Now, let’s talk about what it really takes to keep excellence alive in your organization—not just for a moment, but for the long run.
See, building a culture of excellence isn’t a one-and-done thing. It’s something you nurture, reinforce, and adapt to, every single day.
So, how do you make sure those principles and habits we’ve talked about don’t just fade away? Well, it comes down to a few key practices.
First, let’s think about rituals and routines. These are the regular habits—like recognition ceremonies that shine a spotlight on great work, learning reviews to reflect and improve, or customer listening sessions that keep you connected to what really matters. These little moments keep your core values front and center, day after day.
Then there’s storytelling. Sharing stories of success, challenges, and lessons learned does more than just entertain—it reminds everyone what the organization stands for, and encourages others to step up and do the same. Think about the energy in the room when someone shares how they overcame a tough obstacle, or when a team’s achievements get celebrated. Stories like these inspire and unite.
Leadership development is another big one. When you invest in growing future leaders, you’re making sure that the culture of excellence outlasts any one person or situation. Maybe that means mentoring new employees, or giving rising stars the chance to take on new challenges. Whatever form it takes, you’re handing down not just skills, but the mindset and values that keep the organization strong.
For example, imagine a company that celebrates teams who truly live out its values—a place where the mission and strategy are regularly revisited, making sure they still make sense as things change. Or think about a mentoring program, where experienced folks help newcomers not just learn the ropes, but really understand what the culture is all about.
But here’s something to pay attention to—sustaining excellence means staying alert. It’s easy for complacency or bureaucracy to sneak in, or for people to slowly drift away from what really matters. That’s why it’s so important to ask tough questions, seek honest feedback, and be ready to make changes, even when it’s uncomfortable.
So, what’s the real takeaway here? Excellence isn’t a finish line you cross—it’s a way of being. It’s built from the small choices you and your team make, day after day. When everyone’s committed to doing their best and helping others do the same, that’s when excellence truly becomes part of who you are.
